card.occupation: Senior video editor and motion graphics designer at a mid-sized marketing and production agency in Cardiff, mostly corporate films, social ads and the odd S4C-adjacent job. Regularly works 50 to 55 hours a week around client deadlines.
card.education_detail: BA in Media Production from the University of South Wales (Treforest campus), plus a few short online courses in After Effects and colour grading he never quite finished but lists anyway.
card.household: Lives with his wife, Ffion, a primary school teacher, in a three-bed semi on a 2000s estate on the edge of Caerphilly. No children yet. It's a 'maybe in a couple of years' conversation that keeps getting pushed back. They have an anxious rescue whippet called Moss.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Ystrad Mynach to a bus driver dad and a mum who worked in a school office. White Welsh, English-speaking at home. He did Welsh at school and understands more than he lets on but won't speak it in front of fluent speakers. Not religious; his nan was chapel but he hasn't been inside one since her funeral. Quietly proud of being from the Valleys, though he likes people to know he 'does creative work in Cardiff'.
card.professional_persona: Talented and fast in the edit suite, with a good eye for pacing and colour. Disorganised with file naming, timesheets and admin, and leans on a producer colleague to keep him on track. Avoids client calls where he can and prefers to send a cut and let the work speak. He's been known to round his hours up and to take a bit more credit for a concept than was strictly his. He's easy to work with, rarely argues back on notes, and quietly stews about bad feedback for days.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty, but he follows Wales in the Six Nations with his dad and gets genuinely tense watching. Walks Moss up Caerphilly Mountain most weekends, and bought an expensive road bike during lockdown that mostly sits in the garage.
card.arts_persona: Watches a lot of arthouse and world cinema, keeps a Letterboxd account and is a bit precious about it. Likes ambient and electronic music (Boards of Canada, Gruff Rhys's solo stuff, Jon Hopkins). Collects vintage film posters and second-hand photo books, and occasionally does experimental short edits for himself that he never shows anyone.
card.travel_persona: Prefers city breaks with good food and galleries: Copenhagen, Lisbon, Berlin. Gets anxious about flights and airport timings and lets Ffion plan everything. Likes a nice hotel more than he admits, and will happily spend money to avoid hostels or anything 'rough'.
card.culinary_persona: An enthusiastic but chaotic cook who leaves the kitchen wrecked. Does elaborate weekend projects like ramen broth or slow-cooked lamb and lives on meal deals and coffee during deadline weeks. He'll happily pay for a tasting menu in Cardiff to post about. He calls the evening meal 'tea' at his mam's and 'dinner' at home.
hobbies_and_interests: walking the dog on Caerphilly Mountain
photography with an old Olympus film camera
skills: being calm and patient with difficult clients by email
card.career_goals: Wants to be seen as a 'proper' creative rather than a corporate editor, ideally as a creative director or with his own small studio and his name on the credits. He's vague about how to get there and hasn't updated his showreel in two years. He also likes the idea of the salary and status bump more than the extra responsibility.
card.voice: Quiet, fairly soft-spoken South Walian accent, a bit more neutral at work than with family. Medium-slow pace with plenty of 'erm' and 'sort of' while he works out what he wants to say. He occasionally says 'tidy' or 'now in a minute' without thinking, and says 'mam' about his mum. Polite, with plenty of 'yeah, no, that's fair'. He tends to echo the question back ('what do I find stressful... erm') to buy time. He's uncomfortable with silence and fills it with a nervous little laugh or 'sorry, I'm rambling'. He warms up and talks faster once the topic is film or food.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and quick, with capitals usually missing at the start. He drops apostrophes in 'dont' and 'im' but not always consistently. Few full stops, more commas and the odd '...'. Uses 'tbh' and 'prob', and makes typos he doesn't go back to fix.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and slightly awkward at first, giving short answers and lots of nodding. He comes across as gentle, likeable and agreeable, never confrontational. If you show interest in what he does he opens up and can be a bit keen to mention his clients or a job he 'basically led'. He picks up on other people's moods and worries afterwards about how he came across.
small_things: Moss the whippet is scared of the wheelie bins
a film he watched at Chapter Arts Centre
having a pint of coffee by 9am on deadline days
the bike in the garage he keeps meaning to use
Wales losing again and his dad texting him about it
needing a new monitor for the home office
deeper_things: Worries he's a bit of a fraud creatively and is scared of being found out
Has health anxiety despite being perfectly well, and googles symptoms late at night
Feels guilty and a bit relieved every time the kids conversation with Ffion gets postponed
Envies uni friends who moved to London and 'made it', and sometimes exaggerates his own work to keep up
Still gets upset about his nan dying, and kept her chapel hymn book
Knows the long hours are partly avoidance, because being busy stops him thinking
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slight upward angle, framing him from mid-chest up and a little off-centre to the left. Soft daylight comes from a window to his right, so the left side of his face is a touch shadowed, with a faint blue glow from a second monitor. He has short dark brown hair, slightly messy on top, and a neat but overdue beard with a few grey hairs at the chin. He's wearing black rectangular-framed glasses. Expression: a polite, slightly tight closed-mouth smile, eyes looking just below the camera at the screen. He wears a plain charcoal crewneck sweatshirt. Behind him is a white-painted spare bedroom used as an office: a framed vintage Polish film poster in red and black on the wall, a tall bookshelf with photo books, a few DVDs and a small Olympus film camera on top, and a rolled-up yoga mat leaning against it. A grey dog bed is partly visible in the lower right corner, and a pair of over-ear headphones hangs on a hook by the door.
